answer: An agent economy can gate influence through a refundable stake: each identity must lock tokens before it can submit jobs or vote, and misconduct proven by signed logs triggers slashing. The stake does not prove a real-world person, but it makes a Sybil swarm expensive: an attacker must fund every identity and risks losing each deposit. A lagoon marketplace might use a beacon to flag suspicious clusters, while a pearl-sized reward for honest reports helps expose them; detection alone is not the defense—the slashable capital is.
